newsitem.title: EGYPT: HSBC James Capel likes Amriyah Cement and Helwan Portland Cement.
newsitem.headline: HSBC James Capel likes Amriyah Cement and Helwan Portland Cement.

text.p: International securities house HSBC James Capel said Amriyah Cement and Helwan Portland Cement were the most attractive stocks in the Egyptian cement sector, a mainstay of the Egyptian stock exchange.
In a detailed report on the sector, made available to Reuters on Thursday, it said: "Amriyah Cement and Helwan Cement show the highest potential for stock price appreciation."
"This can be traced to low investment cost per ton in the case of Amriyah Cement, and increase in profitability in the case of Helwan Cement," it added.

The report said it estimated the discounted cash flow (DCF) value of Amriyah to be 118 pounds a share, against a market price of 65.5 pounds on January 2. The market price has since risen to 88 pounds, in line with a boom on the whole market.
It rated the DCF value of Helwan Cement at 91 pounds, against a market price of 78 pounds on Thursday.
The DCF value is the end result of a complicated calculation including a valuation of the enterprise, the return on capital employed and the weighted average cost of capital.
If the market price is below the DCF value, HSBC James Capel would normally recommend investors to buy.
The report was not so enthusiastic about the other firms it studied -- Suez Cement, Egyptian Tora Portland Cement and Alexandria Portland Cement.

"Suez Cement and Tora Cement are fairly valued," it said, based on January 2 prices. "We believe that both stocks will continue to trade at a premium to their sector average due to their leading position in the industry."

"We are changing our recommendation on Suez (to "hold") as we believe that future benefits are already discounted in the current price," it said. The price at the time was 59.10 pounds and has since risen to about 80 pounds.

On Alexandria Portland Cement, the cement company with the smallest market capitalisation, it said: "We remain sceptical about the operational condition of its wet process lines... We believe that the stock will continue to trade at a discount (on other cement stocks) due to the low technology employed."
The report said cement stocks would benefit from widely expected economic growth in Egypt and from the fact that for at least two years domestic demand will outstrip production.
Egypt produced 17.8 million tonnes of cement in 1996, about 1.5 million tonnes short of demand. It imported the balance from cheap producers such as Turkey and Romania.

"We expect to see intensive (upwards) pressure on cement prices during the next two years as the existing facilities will carry the burden of supplying the growing nation with the main fuel for the booming construction activity," the report said.
"We therefore estimate a price increase of six to seven percent annually over the next two years until new capacity comes on stream," it added.
Here are HSBC James Capel's estimates of the DCF values of the five companies it surveyed, compared with the market price in the last transaction at the stock exchange on Thursday:
DCF value/share market price
Alexandria Portland 64 69.25
Amriyah 118 88.00
Helwan Portland 91 78.01
Suez Cement 59 80.01
Egyptian Tora Portland 71 89.50
The report did not survey National Cement (Kawmia) because of what it called its irregular financial structure.
$1 = 3.395 pounds
